The '''Imperial Language Academy''' was the main language authority of the [[Vesperan Empire]]. It supervised official use of the [[Vesperan Language]] and [[Vesperan Alphabet]] across imperial administration, education, diplomacy, law, military records, and ceremonial writing.

== Establishment ==

Source material places the Academy's establishment in 1715, shortly after the [[Imperial Proclamation of 1710]]. The timing fits the early imperial need to turn the older kingdom language into a standardized tool for a larger empire.

The Academy inherited earlier kingdom-era language policy associated with the [[Royal Language Decree of 1652]] and expanded it into a more formal imperial system.

== Responsibilities ==

The Academy regulated official grammar, spelling, formal vocabulary, administrative terminology, and approved script forms. It also helped prepare clerical guides and official language used by imperial ministries.

In practice, this made the Academy a political institution as much as a scholarly one. Standard Vesperan reduced local variation and made imperial records easier to audit from the capital.

== Imperial Policy ==

The Academy's work supported cultural integration policy. Provincial governments and occupation administrations could use its standards to introduce Vesperan in schools, courts, offices, archives, and official correspondence.

This produced uneven results. In some core provinces, standardized Vesperan became a normal administrative language. In occupied regions such as [[Belcanto Nations|Belcanto]] and Veszpremi border districts, the same policy became associated with suppression and resistance.

== Collapse And Legacy ==

The Academy ceased to operate as a state authority when the Vesperan Empire collapsed in 1949. Surviving manuals, dictionaries, grammar texts, and archive practices influenced later scholarship and post-imperial cultural preservation.
